images.prompt: Create a clean educational diagram explaining 5-fold cross-validation. Top section: one horizontal bar labeled 'Full Dataset' divided into exactly 5 equal segments labeled Fold 1, Fold 2, Fold 3, Fold 4, Fold 5. Below it: exactly 5 rows labeled Iteration 1 through Iteration 5. In each row, show the same 5 segments in the same order. In Iteration 1, Fold 1 is red and labeled 'Test Fold'; Folds 2-5 are blue and labeled 'Training Folds'. In Iteration 2, Fold 2 is red (Test Fold) and the other four are blue (Training Folds). Continue this pattern so each iteration uses a different fold as the test fold. Use simple flat colors, crisp sans-serif text, no typos, no duplicate iteration labels, no extra rows, no mind-map styling.

images.prompt: A 2D grid representing hyperparameter tuning. One axis is labeled "Hyperparameter 1 Value" (e.g., C), and the other is "Hyperparameter 2 Value" (e.g., max_iter). Each intersection point on the grid represents a unique combination of hyperparameter values. A color gradient or numerical labels within each cell indicates the model's performance (e.g., accuracy) for that combination, with the "best" combination clearly highlighted.
